theory_point: In medical Latin, the most relevant word classes are nouns, adjectives, numerals, verbs, adverbs, prepositions, and conjunctions
Nouns have masculine (m.), feminine (f.), or neuter (n.) gender
Forms may be singular (sg.) or plural (pl.)
For medical terminology, the most important cases are nominative, genitive, accusative, and ablative
Declension is recognized by the genitive singular ending
I: -ae, II: -i, III consonant: -is, III vowel: -is, IV: -us, V: -ei
The stem is obtained by removing the genitive singular ending
The adjective must agree with the noun in case, gender, and number
Without a preposition, the second noun is usually in the genitive and functions as a non-agreeing attribute
A preposition requires a specific case; some, such as in and sub, may take accusative or ablative depending on meaning
